subject: Performance SLO & customer-led load test coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finwise.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & load test coordination

Hi Alex - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned on the load test plan: 

Summary of SLOs discussed:
- Latency targets: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 350ms for server-side responses (for non-streaming requests)
- Streaming requirements: token-level streaming with first-token latency < 150ms and steady per-token latency targets (we discussed chunked SSE responses)
- Throughput/concurrency: goal is a sustained throughput equivalent to 200 RPS with bursts to 400 RPS; concurrency target 250 concurrent sessions

Load-test coordination items (proposed):
1) Customer to run load test using their k6/Locust harness (you mentioned k6) and share the script.
2) We'll provide a test API key and a set of IPs to allowlist.
3) Suggest test window: Thu 2026-07-22 02:00-05:00 UTC (redwood infra team available) - confirm if that works for you.
4) Engineering checks: Redwood will disable autoscaling on the dedicated test pool for the run, expose Prometheus/metrics endpoint for the run, and capture request/response timings and model-level token metrics.
5) Post-test: collect k6 artifacts, Prometheus metrics, and a short regression summary vs. your SLOs.

Ask: Can you confirm the test window and attach the k6 script you plan to run (or paste the critical parts that simulate streaming)? Once we have the script we'll validate it against our test account and provide allowlist IPs.

Thanks - I'll coordinate infra on our side once you confirm.

- Marissa

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finwise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: QA Team <qa@finwise.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & load test coordination

Thanks Marissa - recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side + attached k6 script (k6_loadtest_v1.js):

- Confirmed SLOs: p50 < 100ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 350ms for standard API calls. Streaming: first-token < 150ms, per-token target ~30ms.
- Throughput: our target is 200 RPS sustained on the route that fans out to the model pool; we may run a burst phase up to 450 RPS to validate graceful degradation.
- Concurrency: expect roughly 220 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Test window: Thu 2026-07-22 02:00-05:00 UTC works for our dev/QA team. Please provide test account/credentials and IP allowlist at least 48 hours in advance.

Attached: k6_loadtest_v1.js (simulates streaming by splitting payloads and using a sleep between chunks).

Also: We'll need an endpoint to scrape Prometheus metrics (or you can push a link to the raw metrics after the run).

Let me know if Redwood needs any changes to the script (e.g., different header usage, longer think times).

- Alex
Alex Chen

Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & load test coordination

Hi Alex - thanks for the script, I reviewed it quickly and it looks fine to exercise our API patterns. A few operational details and the test account info below.

Test account / access:
- API key: rw_test_key_finwise_2026 (note: we'll send the real key via the secure portal; this is the label)
- Test tenant id: finwise-loadtest-2026
- Rate-limit override: we'll apply a temporary override for the run to allow the requested RPS/connection counts.

Allowlist IPs (please confirm these are acceptable on your side):
- 34.201.10.45/32
- 34.201.11.12/32
- 34.201.12.76/32

Notes / questions:
- Streaming: the k6 script appears to simulate streaming by chunked POSTs. If you need true long-lived SSE connections we can provide an endpoint that returns chunked SSE and we'll record first-byte latency. Please confirm whether your harness will open long-lived connections for streaming or will emulate streaming via sequential requests.
- Autoscaling: we will disable autoscaling for the dedicated test pool during the 3-hour window to get stable behavior; we'll re-enable autoscaling once the test artifacts are collected.
- Metrics: I will expose a Prometheus scrape endpoint for the run at https://metrics.redwood.com/scrape/finwise-loadtest-2026 (read-only for your team).

Attached: test_account_details.txt (contains the setup checklist and internal runbook references).

If everything looks good we'll provision the key and allowlists by Tue 2026-07-20 09:00 UTC.

- Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Alex - quick note from the infra/observability side:
- We'll capture request latency histograms at the router and at the model-serving layer, plus token generation timing where available.
- I'll disable background sampling jobs and warm the model cache for 30 minutes pre-test to reduce cold-start noise.
- Post-run I'll produce a short artifact with: k6 summary, Prometheus dashboards (PNG), and a bullet list of any observed throttles/errors.

If you need any additional metrics (e.g., GPU utilization per model shard) please flag and we'll include them.

- Rishi
